title: Identification of section comparisons on an etale upper tail
statement: Let I be a preorder, R a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], B : I opposite -> R.Etale a diagram [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and c any cone of its underlying scheme diagram. Let p : c.pt -> R and assume each cone leg followed by its stage structure map is p. Let H be a sheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], i0 an index, and nu a natural transformation to the sections of p inverse image H at the terminal etale object whose components are the inverse-image unit [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] followed by restriction along the diagonal pullback lift [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put D equal to the underlying scheme diagram, G equal to the inverse image of H along the structure map at i0, and W0 equal to the terminal etale object over D(i0). For every j in Over(i0 opposite), there exist isomorphisms a_j from H(B_j) to the sections of D(j.hom) inverse image G on the base change of W0, and an isomorphism l from the nu vertex to the sections of the cone-leg-at-i0 inverse image G on the limit-base-change object. For every arrow f : k -> j over i0, H(B(f) opposite) followed by a_k equals a_j followed by the canonical transition section comparison [def-weil-pbc-sets-section-comparison]. Moreover nu_j followed by l equals a_j followed by the canonical cone section comparison. No directedness, qcqs, affine-transition, or limit hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put D equal to the underlying scheme diagram, G equal to the inverse image of H at i0, and W0 equal to its terminal etale object. The over-morphism equations give D(j.hom) followed by the stage-i0 structure morphism equal to the stage-j structure morphism. Apply unit-compatible inverse-image composition and equality transport to identify the iterated inverse image with the inverse image of H along the stage-j structure morphism.

The pullback of the identity object W0 is isomorphic to the terminal etale object at stage j: its second projection is an isomorphism with inverse the pullback lift of the structure map and identity. Evaluate the sheaf-composition isomorphism and then etale restriction at that terminal object. Restriction there is H(Bj); invert the composite to obtain a_j. The same identity-pullback and composition construction along the cone leg at i0 gives the limit-point isomorphism l, using h i0 to identify its composite with p. This needs no etaleness of p or cone legs.

For k to j over i0, expand the canonical section comparison into unit, chosen composition isomorphism, equality transport, and pullback pasting. Move a pulled-back section through it by unit naturality and the composition-unit equation. Under etale restriction the section becomes H on the opposite stage morphism. The two pasting maps have identical pullback projections, so they agree. This proves H(B(f).op) followed by a_k equals a_j followed by the section comparison.

Repeat the composition-unit calculation for the cone leg at j. The pullback map has first projection c_j and second projection the identity, so pullback uniqueness identifies it with the explicit diagonal lift in hnu. Thus nu at j followed by l equals a_j followed by the cone section comparison. These are isomorphism and naturality statements for any cone, not a continuity or colimit assertion.
